newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Rescuers speak to Australian ski lodge survivor.
newsitem.headline: Rescuers speak to Australian ski lodge survivor.

text.p: Rescuers have spoken to a man who is buried in the wreckage of two Australian ski lodges engulfed by a landslide more than two days ago, police said on Saturday.
"They have made voice contact with a male person and he is certainly alive," a police spokesman said.
"A miracle has occurred...," police chief superintendent Charlie Sanderson told reporters at a news conference.

Police had earlier suspended the rescue operation, fearing another landslide, but renewed the operation after about 20 minutes when ambulance workers crawled under a concrete slab to try to reach the survivor.
"Ambulance officers are in the cavity, some metres from reaching him," said Sanderson, adding police hoped to pull the man out shortly.
The landslide occurred just before midnight on Wednesday at Thredbo, 400 km (250 miles) south of Sydney, Australia's most popular skiing resort.
